match.reason: The closest bank point covers Australia's general flatness and the Great Dividing Range, but it does not teach the Central Lowlands or the Western Plateau or the idea that Australia is old, so it is related rather than the same idea.

draft.title: Australia's major landforms
card: Australia is the lowest and flattest inhabited continent. Its land is very old, and wind and water have worn it down over a very long time.
Great Dividing Range
a long chain of highlands down the east coast. It is the main mountain region of the continent.
Central Lowlands
a low, flat area in the middle of the continent. It lies west of the Great Dividing Range.
Western Plateau
a large, high, flat area covering most of the west. It is the biggest of the three regions.
draft.remember: Australia is old, low and flat. Highlands lie in the east, lowlands in the middle and a plateau across the west.

a.q: Which landform region covers most of the west of Australia?
opts: The Western Plateau
The Central Lowlands
The Great Dividing Range
The east coast highlands
a.why: The Western Plateau is a large, flat area that covers most of the west. The Central Lowlands are tempting, but they lie in the middle of the continent, not across the west.
a.clue: Think of the largest region, in the west.

b.q: Sam travels from the east coast of Australia to the far west. Which order of landform regions does he cross?
opts: Great Dividing Range, Central Lowlands, Western Plateau
Western Plateau, Central Lowlands, Great Dividing Range
Central Lowlands, Great Dividing Range, Western Plateau
Great Dividing Range, Western Plateau, Central Lowlands
b.why: The Great Dividing Range lies in the east, the Central Lowlands are in the middle and the Western Plateau covers most of the west. The reverse order is tempting, but it describes a trip from west to east.
b.clue: Start with the highlands in the east, then move west.

wants.brief: A simple map of Australia showing three labelled regions: the Great Dividing Range in the east, the Central Lowlands in the middle and the Western Plateau across most of the west.
wants.why: Seeing where each region sits helps students remember their order from east to west.

b.best: Great Dividing Range, Central Lowlands, Western Plateau

problems.detail: The question asks which region covers 'most of the west', and the right option is the only one named 'Western'. Together with a clue that says 'in the west', a student can pick it from the wording alone, without knowing the idea.

proposal.title: Australia's major landforms
card: Australia is the lowest and flattest inhabited continent. Its land is very old, and over a very long time wind and water have worn it down. That is why so much of it is low and flat.
Great Dividing Range
a long chain of highlands down the east coast. It is the main mountain region of the continent.
Central Lowlands
a low, flat area in the middle of the continent. It lies west of the Great Dividing Range.
Western Plateau
a large, raised, flat area covering most of the west. It is the biggest of the three regions.
proposal.remember: Australia is old, low and flat. Highlands lie in the east, lowlands in the middle and a plateau across the west.

a.q: Most of Australia is low and flat. What is the main reason for this?
opts: Its old land has been worn down by wind and water
Its young land has not yet had time to rise up
Ice sheets have pressed its land flat over time
Volcanoes have spread lava flat across its land
a.why: Australia's land is very old, so wind and water have had a very long time to wear it down. The idea of young land is tempting, but it reverses the truth: Australia is low and flat because its land is old, not young.
a.clue: Think about how long the land has been exposed to the weather.

b.q: Sam travels from the east coast of Australia to the far west. Which order of landform regions does he cross?
opts: Great Dividing Range, Central Lowlands, Western Plateau
Western Plateau, Central Lowlands, Great Dividing Range
Central Lowlands, Great Dividing Range, Western Plateau
Great Dividing Range, Western Plateau, Central Lowlands
b.why: The Great Dividing Range lies in the east, the Central Lowlands are in the middle and the Western Plateau covers most of the west. The reverse order is tempting, but it describes a trip from west to east.
b.clue: Start with the highlands in the east, then move west.
